text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Hanoi Mayor Hoang Van Nghien has called on party members and municipal authorities to follow the lessons learnt 50 years ago in the battle for control of Hanoi, relying firmly on national solidarity and unity to develop the capital city.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Khanh praised the worldwide work of the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (UNICEF) during a meeting with the fund's honorary spokesperson and famour singer, Nana Mouskouri.
-- British finance group CDC has approved a loan of $15 million for the construction of a sugar plant in southern Vietnam.
-- More than two million private businesses throughout the country will have to re-register their activities in 1997.
-- Two 15-year-old boys were given 15-month and 24-month suspended prison sentences by the Hanoi People's Court for drug abuse.
-- Japanese direct investment in Vietnam between April and September increased by 430 percent compared with the same period of last year.
-- Ho Chi Minh City's Communist Party Committee has called for thrift during the Tet lunar new year festival in February.
